one_liner: Senior cybersecurity leadership talent pool at DHS: leading cyber incident response, threat monitoring, and vulnerability mitigation teams across CISA, FEMA, ICE, and others.
fit_summary: This role requires 5-15 years of hands-on cybersecurity work experience plus a proctored technical cyber assessment, and the resume review explicitly checks for cybersecurity experience. Nothing on file shows Daniel has a technical cyber background, so emergency-management consulting at IEM and policy knowledge won't substitute. Daniel would likely pass Phase I's non-technical simulations but stall at Phase II.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); no federal status or veterans' preference required.
Leadership Track expects 5-15 years of cybersecurity work experience and up to 5 years of cybersecurity leadership; the resume must explicitly outline cybersecurity experience.
Must obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI (Sensitive Compartmented Information) clearance.
No degree required, but you will answer education questions.
Must pass all three assessment phases, including a proctored Mitigation and Response technical exam at an assessment center.
strategy: Be honest with yourself first: apply only if you have real cybersecurity work (e.g., cyber incident planning, IT security exercises) at IEM or elsewhere; otherwise skip this one.
If IEM work touched cyber (cyber tabletop exercises, critical infrastructure resilience, continuity plans), state those duties explicitly with dates and hours per week within the two-page limit.
Translate emergency-management language into posting terms: after-action reports, recovery action plans, stakeholder coordination, and communications tailored to leadership audiences.
Block 3+ hours with a reliable computer and audio for Phase I, and watch email closely; assessments are time-sensitive.
Apply between Oct 15 and Oct 30, 2026; better-fit alternatives are FEMA emergency management (0089) or DHS/CISA policy and external affairs roles that value IEM and policy experience.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [type] preparedness/recovery support for [government client] at IEM, producing [number] after-action reports and recovery action plans tailored to [audience, e.g., agency leadership]. ([dates], [hours]/week)
Facilitated [cyber/all-hazards] tabletop exercises with [number] stakeholders from [agencies/sectors], documenting gaps and recommending mitigation strategies adopted in [plan/result].
Briefed [level of leadership] on incident status, impact, and next steps during [event/exercise], customizing communications for [audiences].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you led a team through a cyber incident using NIST incident handling stages.
How would you communicate a major incident's status and impact to senior leadership versus SOC staff?
Describe a time you performed root cause analysis and drove a recovery action plan to completion.
How have you used SIEM or log data to identify a threat?
watch_outs: Core requirement is years of hands-on cybersecurity experience Daniel likely lacks; the resume review confirms it after Phase II.
TS/SCI clearance required, which means a lengthy background investigation.
No telework, short 15-day window, and selection is from a talent pool, so hiring timing is uncertain.
